explanation: The central figure in the gospel who teaches about God's kingdom, performs miracles, and is revealed as the Messiah.
A basic element of food that Jesus uses to feed thousands of people through a miracle.
One of the few food items available to the group before the great meal, symbolizing human lack and God's abundance.
A physical condition that Jesus heals to demonstrate his divine power and authority.
The concept of both physical sight and the deeper spiritual insight the disciples must develop to understand Jesus' identity.
A title Jesus uses for himself referring to his role in God's plan, often associated with suffering and future glory.
The symbol of the coming death and the sacrifice Jesus must take to fulfill prophecies about the Messiah.
The description of those who refuse to follow Jesus' path by prioritizing worldly things over God's kingdom, which leads to eternal loss.
